newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The Bank of Greece lent its voice yesterday to the government's intention to change the status quo in the job market and social security system, with central bank governor Lucas Papademos calling on the government and other bodies to make immediate decisions through dialogue.

--Talks on the fate of the social insurance system will begin in June while the labour and social security ministry is preparing a series of immediate measures that will be contained in an omnibus bill.

--Papademos recommended radical structural change to all economic sectors - the job market, pension funds, banks and the market for goods and services - that will ensure Greece finds itself on the road to real convergence and ready for inclusion in the euro in 2001.

--A new presidential decree will lend the SDOE economic crimes squad new powers, following a draft decree submitted to the Council of State. The long hand of the SDOE will be able to reach into state procurements contracts, state subsidies and private capital to detect irregularities.
--Exchange policy has achieved its mission, the central bank governor said yesterday, and the current mix of economic policies needs to be improved on.
--The pace of fiscal reform needs to be stepped up and expanded, with the emphasis on controls and cut backs in state spending and all spending in all public bodies, Papademos added.
--March saw a four-year record in unemployment figures, OECD said yesterday. The rate was 9.24 percent (227,052), an increase of 0.77 percent over March 1996 figures.
--The finance ministry yesterday offered taxpayers another chance to settle outstanding debts from the 1983-1992 period.
--The domestic leasing market is leaping ahead with a 20 percent growth rate, creating large profit margins for firms active in the sector.

--Growth needs a trimmer state, is the message from yesterday's presentation of the central bank's report on the economy. The economy has seen positive developments but these have not yet created the conditions to maitain growth, Papademos stressed.
--The finance ministry will issue two-year zero coupons for public subscription in early May. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
